findings.title: Placeholder crop images with empty alt
findings.detail: Design mock uses empty alt on crop images and static placeholder counts; if this is only a design ref that is expected, but production UI cannot ship empty-alt decorative-or-content crop marks without real alt text. This chunk only shows the design-ref HTML, not production components—cannot verify production a11y from this patch alone for that path. More critically: INTEGRATIONS.md is truncated mid-sentence in the provided patch text, so completeness of that file cannot be verified from the message body alone.

findings.title: Touch targets fail WCAG minimum
findings.detail: header-build-measure.json records repeated touchFails on mobile and desktop: many anchors (including source-link) are only 21px tall (well under the 44px WCAG 2.5.5 / mobile UX minimum). This is measured evidence of undersized interactive controls, not a clean pass.

findings.title: First timeline cell not above the fold
findings.detail: Every measured frame reports firstTimelineCellVisible: false (light-375, dark-375, light-1280, dark-1280, drawer-open, paint viewports). Search and title are above the fold, but the primary calendar grid content is not verified as visible in the initial viewport.

findings.title: Mobile header far taller than mockup budget
findings.detail: Mockup budget headerHeight375 is 452 vs measured headerHeight 127 when drawer closed — that looks like an improvement — but light-375-drawer-open reports headerHeight 508, which exceeds the mockup header budget and pushes timelineTop to 508 with timelineSpaceAboveFold only 336. Drawer-open mobile layout still consumes most of the viewport for chrome.

findings.title: paint field null on primary frames
findings.detail: light-375, dark-375, light-1280, dark-1280, and light-375-drawer-open all set paint: null. Only paint-1440 reports a ratio (~0.993). Theme/paint coverage is incomplete for the standard 375/1280 light/dark matrix; cannot verify light/dark canvas paint from those frames.

findings.title: resolveZone name match is non-deterministic and over-broad
findings.detail: resolveZone falls through to `WHERE name LIKE ?` with `%q%` and `LIMIT 1` ordered only by name. A short city fragment (e.g. "mesa") can match multiple zones; the chosen row is whichever sorts first alphabetically, not the best match. That is silent wrong-zone resolution for calendar APIs that depend on resolveZoneParam.

findings.title: listZones AZ/Arizona filter hardcodes name patterns only
findings.detail: State search for `az`/`arizona` matches only fixed LIKE patterns on `name` (`% AZ %`, `%Arizona%`, etc.). Zones that store state only in other columns (or names that do not embed ` AZ ` / `Arizona`) will be omitted. County/zip/id paths are fine; the state special-case is fragile and unverified against actual seed name formats in this chunk.

findings.title: WINDOW_MONTH_OVERLAP year-wrap logic is weak / possibly wrong
findings.detail: For wrapping windows (`start_half_month > end_half_month`), the predicate ORs four half bounds without clearly relating them to the two halves of the requested month. Compared to the non-wrapping branches (which test overlap of [start,end] with each half of the month), the wrap branch can include windows that do not actually overlap the requested month, or miss edge cases. Cannot verify correctness without tests/data in this chunk; treat as FAIL until proven.

findings.title: guideToApi has no return type
findings.detail: guideToApi is exported without an explicit return type. Under TypeScript strict projects this is weaker API surface than the surrounding typed helpers; callers can drift. Minor, but the new public helper should declare its shape.

findings.title: feature-audit crawler does not exercise interaction-only controls
findings.detail: The crawl only scans static roles on listed routes; it does not open menus, expand dialogs, or change theme. Stale entries require whyNotCrawled, which is good fail-closed policy, but any control only reachable after interaction will either fail audit or be excused without a functional test unless a separate e2e claims it. The PASS message claims every interactive control is tested; that is only true if the manifest + e2e set is complete — not verifiable from this script alone.

findings.title: escapeLike used consistently; parameterized SQL verified
findings.detail: User search fragments for crops/zones go through escapeLike and bound parameters with ESCAPE '\'. getWindowsForHalf/getAllWindows use fixed SQL shapes rather than interpolating method/month into the string. That part of the chunk is sound for SQL injection.

findings.title: Crop guides never invent missing fields
findings.detail: getCropGuide returns null when no row exists; CropGuideRow null fields are documented as source-omitted. guideToApi passes them through without defaults. Design matches the stated anti-invention rule.

findings.title: viewport never applied in measure()
findings.detail: measure() accepts width/height and the outer loop iterates 375/1280/1440/1920, but newContext() is called with no viewport and page.setViewportSize is never called. Every run captures the browser default size; searchCountY, paintedPct, screenshots, and truncation probes are therefore not measured at the claimed breakpoints. FAIL: multi-viewport claims are unverifiable from this script.

findings.title: theme not set via colorScheme/emulation
findings.detail: Theme is only forced via localStorage + data-theme after load. Playwright colorScheme is never set, so prefers-color-scheme media queries and any CSS that depends on them are not measured. Combined with fixed viewport omission, light/dark × size matrix evidence is weak.

findings.title: fixed wait instead of ready signal
findings.detail: await page.waitForTimeout(250) after theme flip is a fixed sleep, not a paint/layout ready signal. Metrics (axe, bounding boxes, truncation) can run before styles settle; protocol requires real ready signals.

findings.title: touch target check weakens WCAG 44px
findings.detail: Code detects r.height < 44 || r.width < 44 then only reports if r.height < 40, and never requires width ≥ 44. Narrow or short controls can pass the probe while failing a real 44×44 touch target gate.

findings.title: paintCoverage samples only opaque bg/text
findings.detail: Paint ratio counts elementFromPoint cells with non-transparent backgroundColor or non-empty text color. Gradient/image backgrounds, canvas, and SVG paint can be under-counted; transparent parents with painted children at sample points can skew ratio. Do not treat ratio as proof of full-viewport theme paint without screenshots reviewed.

findings.title: footer 2-col grid on mobile may hurt readability
findings.detail: site-footer uses grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr even on phone, with comment that lists are short. Legal/nav links stay min-height touch but columns stay narrow; risk of cramped labels or wrap. Not proven broken without screenshot, but mobile-first stacked footer is the safer default—verify visually before claiming done.

findings.title: topbar zone/nav visibility only at 900px+
findings.detail: Desktop topbar zone and nav show at min-width 900px; menu button hidden. Intermediate tablet widths (e.g. 768) may still rely on hamburger—acceptable if intentional, but chunk provides no evidence drawer remains accessible and labeled. Not a hard fail if mobile menu exists; incomplete verification in this patch alone.

findings.title: measurement scripts are evidence producers not product tests
findings.detail: These scripts write JSON/screenshots when run; the patch does not include committed measure JSON, screenshots, or CI wiring proving they ran green. Presence of measure scripts ≠ verified UX. Without artifacts in this chunk, product-quality claims backed only by these files FAIL verification.

findings.title: navClass signature mismatch
findings.detail: PrimaryNavLinks is passed className={navClass}, but navClass was changed from ({ isActive }) => string to (isActive: boolean) => string. If PrimaryNavLinks still expects a NavLink-style className callback receiving { isActive }, this is a type/runtime contract break; if it now expects (isActive: boolean), that must be verified in PrimaryNavLinks (not fully shown as matching). The Layout change alone makes the old NavLink usage invalid and the new prop shape is only safe if PrimaryNavLinks was updated consistently.

findings.title: Home hides chrome: assistant/theme/zone only off-home
findings.detail: Top bar, breadcrumbs, ZoneSelector, ThemeToggle, and AssistantPanel are gated with !isHome. Comment claims Home uses CompactHeader for brand/nav, but this patch does not prove home still exposes zone selection, theme toggle, primary nav, or assistant. If home lacks those, core product controls regress on the main entry route. Fail until CompactHeader is verified to cover them.

findings.title: Footer legal nav lost privacy/terms prominence pattern ok; terms/privacy only in bottom
findings.detail: Legal links moved to footer bottom only; about/contact remain. Not a hard defect if intentional, but /terms and /privacy remain linked. No fail solely for restructure.

findings.title: LegalPage plain-text only no rich content
findings.detail:
Sections render body as a single

and optional string list items. Acceptable for structured legal copy if callers supply real sections; cannot verify substance of Terms/Privacy content from this file alone. Component itself is fine.

findings.title: useTheme cycle fix is sound
findings.detail: cycle() now reads storage via readThemeMode(), applies applyThemeMode(next) eagerly, then setModeState(next). Addresses stale React state vs localStorage drift so toggle does not appear dead when next equals current React state. Logic is coherent given the comment.

findings.title: ZoneProvider default hardcodes one ZIP
findings.detail: DEFAULT_ZONE_ID = 'zone-cave-creek-85331' is a fixed default; acceptable if product default, but if zones API omits that id, fallback is zones[0]. setZone writes localStorage without guarding SSR beyond getItem; setItem is try/catch. Loading path leaves zone null until zonesPayload arrives — consumers must handle null.

findings.title: LiveSearch CSS uses design tokens
findings.detail: Background/color use var(--surface), var(--text), var(--accent), var(--focus) rather than hardcoded theme paint. No hardcoded light/dark colors visible in the provided CSS hunk.

findings.title: Cannot verify BrandLogo is real artwork
findings.detail: Layout comment claims BrandLogo uses public/brand-mark.png finalized artwork, but BrandLogo implementation and asset are not in this patch. Placeholder/emoji brand cannot be refuted or confirmed here — FAIL verification of real brand mark from this chunk alone for the claim; component swap from text AZ mark is present.

findings.title: plantable-now hash link may miss SPA home
findings.detail: Footer uses <a href="/#plantable-now"> instead of React Router Link. From non-home routes this does a full navigation to /#plantable-now which usually works; from SPA context it can still force reload depending on host. Minor; not a hard fail if hash target exists on HomePage. Existence of id=plantable-now not in this patch.

findings.title: navOpen not closed on route change outside PrimaryNavLinks
findings.detail: navOpen state only closes via onNavigate on PrimaryNavLinks. Browser back, breadcrumb, logo, or theme click leave menu open if PrimaryNavLinks was not the navigation path. If logo is BrandLogo without onNavigate hookup, mobile menu can stay open after leaving. Risk of sticky open overlay on mobile.

findings.title: Footer brand still Cave Creek-only while app expanded
findings.detail: footer.brandBlurb still says 'Free low-desert planting calendar for Cave Creek, Arizona 85331' while appTagline, plantable.subtitle, zone copy, and grid pageLede reframe coverage as Maricopa County low desert with multiple covered towns. That leaves the footer marketing line narrower and inconsistent with the rest of the product copy in this same chunk.

findings.title: Assistant empty state still Cave Creek-only
findings.detail: assistant.empty is 'Type a question about what to plant in Cave Creek.' while assistant.subtitle and zone messaging describe Maricopa County low desert coverage generally. Same coverage-scope mismatch as the footer blurb.

findings.title: Light hero tokens flipped; cannot verify paint
findings.detail: Light-theme hero tokens change from dark paint (#0e1419 bg, light text) to light surface (#f4f6f8 bg, #0e1419 text). Intent looks correct for light-mode hero, but this judge has only the CSS patch—no screenshots or computed styles—so contrast/regression at the hero cannot be verified as passing. FAIL for lack of evidence, not a proven contrast bug.

findings.title: forceThemeMode can miss target mode
findings.detail: forceThemeMode clicks the theme toggle at most 4 times and then asserts data-theme-mode equals the target. With three modes and nextThemeMode skipping indistinguishable steps, reaching a specific mode (especially system after light/dark) can require the loop to land correctly; if the control's data-theme-mode attribute lags a click or the skip logic changes order, the final expect fails flakily rather than retrying until ready. More importantly, the helper never waits for data-theme paint after a click—only the attribute—so theme screenshot evidence may capture an intermediate paint even when the attribute matches.

findings.title: Theme tests do not cover invalid storage values
findings.detail: readThemeMode default and applyThemeMode persistence are tested for light/dark/system, but there is no test for corrupt/unknown localStorage values (e.g. 'auto', empty string, or the prior key 'az-planting-theme'). STORAGE_KEY was renamed from 'az-planting-theme' to 'theme' in theme.ts; existing users keep the old key and silently fall through to the new light default with no migration or regression test. That is a real behavior change with no verification in this chunk.

findings.title: Hero contrast check uses hand-rolled luma, not axe
findings.detail: isDarkRgb parses only simple rgb/rgba() and uses a fixed luma < 40 threshold. getComputedStyle can return color(srgb ...), lab(), or named colors; those return false and can make lightHeroBg/darkHeroBg comparison vacuous (both 'not dark') while still asserting inequality. This is a known-fragile contrast/theme measurement pattern; it does not prove WCAG or that the light theme hero is not near-black.

findings.title: Wrangler AI binding added with no tests in this patch
findings.detail: wrangler.toml adds [ai] binding = "AI". This chunk shows no functions/** usage test, no env type update, and no acceptance coverage for any AI route. Cannot verify the binding is wired, typed, or used safely—fails closed for unverified config surface.

findings.title: API 404 acceptance depends on middleware not shown
findings.detail: New tests require unmatched /api/* to return 404 JSON with error containing 'no such endpoint', and listed routes to return 200 JSON. The implementing middleware/functions code is not in this chunk; the tests document the intended fix but this patch alone does not prove production middleware was corrected—only that tests expect it. Per judge rules, cannot PASS the fix from tests alone without the route handler diff present here.

findings.title: Viewport hero assertion weakened
findings.detail: Hero visibility-in-viewport was relaxed from strict beInViewport() to scrollIntoViewIfNeeded + ratio 0.01, and list viewport check was removed. That can pass when the plantable hero is almost entirely off-screen after layout changes that put the timeline first. The test no longer enforces that plantable content is the above-the-fold hero; it only requires a 1% intersection after forced scroll.

findings.title: nextThemeMode loop always returns a mode even if all match
findings.detail: If resolveTheme were broken so all three modes resolved the same, the for-loop exhausts and returns the last candidate without guaranteeing a visual change. The comment claims 'at most one skip is ever needed' but the code does not assert or fail closed if all candidates match currentResolved—it silently returns a no-op candidate. Unit tests only cover happy paths with working matchMedia stubs.

findings.title: Vitest coverage include narrows to lib/theme/functions
findings.detail: Coverage include is intentionally limited to src/lib/**, src/theme.ts, and functions/** so components do not drag coverage to 0%. That is a reasonable policy and matches the comment; no defect found in the config itself. Theme unit tests cover cycle, default light, system persist, and data-theme attributes.

findings.title: Tailwind v4 Vite plugin registered
findings.detail: Adds @tailwindcss/vite to plugins. No package.json or CSS entry changes appear in this chunk; if dependency/CSS entry were missing elsewhere the build would fail, but this file change alone is correct for Tailwind v4 Vite integration. No explicit defect in the hunk.
